Is it better to put it in your roster so he can give experience and you can more control his evolution. Or should you let your young in the young team to let them develop them peacefully ?
[2025-12-23 20:21] shackleton1892 : Williamson could be a solid bottom line player for GB some day.
[2025-12-23 20:34] rjs_lu_ridware_rangers : It depends on a number of things. 1. If you want to be competitive in your pro team it might be a bad idea 2. You will use his ELC contract years when he isn't really contributing to the team 3. He will earn more experience and that will pay off later in his career (if he's still on your team) 4.  You can control and focus his training but it won't change his end stats 5. Coaches have an impact too.  Your pro coaches may be more focussed on match performance than training.  If your farm or U21 coaches are better at training then they might develop quicker if you don't promote them, but at the expense of experience

[2026-03-01 16:57] rojo6176 : I have maybe again a stupid question, but the sum of my players for example Papez, if we sum we have 41, so his ratings his 55, that means diff of 14, it's the hidden stats is it not ? But when I check the max, and I do again the calculation I arrive at 72, but the max of the ratings is now 82, how the 14 becomes 10 ?
[2026-03-01 17:55] rjs_lu_ridware_rangers : No it's slightly more complicated than that.  I can't remember the exact calculation, but I think it works out the average and each puck that is higher than the average counts as 2.  So two different players with the same number of pucks can have different ratings.  A player with a lot of bad stats and one high one can have a higher ovr than a player with no real strengths or weaknesses.
[2026-03-01 18:06] rjs_lu_ridware_rangers : Here is an example of two players, both have 72ovr. The bald guy on my team has very even stats (no major strengths or weaknesses) and has 62 pucks.  The other guy has lots of 9s but also lots of 4s, he only has a total of 59 pucks.  This means that he has more pucks over the average and this inflates the ovr rating.

[2022-03-01 08:07] hnadmin : This is for 2 reasons. First one is to give some time to trade board to analyse the trade. The board has 24 hours.  Second reason is to ensure that the listed projected salary changes do not depend on the time of approval by board. For instance, suppose GM accepted a trade 1 hour before the daily update, and board approved it just before the daily update. In this case there is only 1 salary day in play instead of the 2 that were used in the calculated projected salary change. Hence, trades always take place on the second daily update after the trade was accepted by the GM.

[2022-07-03 10:11] d0ghouse : With the "For Lines" you can limit which lines the instruction is active for
[2022-07-03 10:11] d0ghouse : if you don't assign any then it's for all lines
[2022-07-03 10:11] diamond_ace : perfect i now have 3 friendlies
[2022-07-03 10:12] d0ghouse : Similar with "Against". This is useful if you only want to change a setting against a specific opponent's line
[2022-07-03 10:13] d0ghouse : "When" allows you to only trigger an instruction at a specific score (example when leading)
[2022-07-03 10:13] d0ghouse : and the "Then" section is used to make the changes to your playing style
[2022-07-03 10:14] d0ghouse : Basically you can combine these settings to make an instruction as specific of global as you want
[2022-07-03 10:17] d0ghouse : for example, if you want to set an instruction for your 1st line D you can select all of these
[2022-07-03 10:19] d0ghouse : You can be as specific as you want. Could make an instruction that only works when your 1st line D is playing with your bottom 6 forwards against the opponent top line for example
[2022-07-03 10:20] sedinery : So for an example, if I set it like this, does that means my first line will play only against opposition first forward line?
[2022-07-03 10:20] d0ghouse : no
[2022-07-03 10:21] d0ghouse : it means the instruction is only active when your line 1 D is playing against the opponents top forwards line
[2022-07-03 10:21] d0ghouse : regardless of the other players on the ice (your forwards and opponent's defense)
[2022-07-03 10:22] d0ghouse : the changes made by the instruction are always the last part
[2022-07-03 10:23] d0ghouse : it enables you to change your default team playing style under specific conditions
[2022-07-03 10:23] d0ghouse : do you have an example in mind of what you want to achieve? You can send me a PM and i can help you with it

[2022-07-07 19:32] dalfsendragons : What does the training performance in daily log actually mean? Does a player level up once it reaches 100%?
[2022-07-07 19:45] d0ghouse : No, it means how effective he was that day
[2022-07-07 20:14] leafs1997 : Is that info useful tho...?
[2022-07-07 20:17] d0ghouse : Yes, because it shows something about the player's work ethic
[2022-07-07 20:22] d0ghouse : Two players with the same kind of potential are not guaranteed to reach the end of their development at the same time. One could end up maxing his skills much later if he doesn't have good work ethic.
[2022-07-07 20:26] d0ghouse : By taking age, current skill level and training speed into account, you will know which players train faster and thus reach their full potential earlier in their careers. Do keep in mind that in general F > D > G when it comes to training speed, because of the difference in number of puck skill categories.
[2022-07-07 20:26] d0ghouse : Here's a quick example:
[2022-07-07 20:27] d0ghouse : Two forwards aged 20, one is training a level 1 skill and the other a level 5 skill.
[2022-07-07 20:27] d0ghouse : The one training the level 5 skill is training faster, despite the skill already being stronger.
[2022-07-07 20:28] d0ghouse : I hope that helps clear up any misunderstandings 👍

[2022-07-08 03:10] chimkintendies : Stupid question — is there a way that you can get an idea of what a players “potential” will be? Besides maybe their draft ranking? If I get a player that has a bunch of non-maxed skills, do I just have to take a risk that they don’t max at 4?
[2022-07-08 03:21] c0ntrail : Look at their listed strongest talents, compare them to the highest maxed talent.  If one of the strongest talents are maxed, its fair to expect the other talent will be about the same
[2022-07-08 03:24] c0ntrail : Like if one talent is maxed at 6, but it's not a strongest talent, then the strongest talents are gonna be 7+.  If the weakest talent is more than 4, then that's a good sign too bc it means everything will be higher than that
[2022-07-08 08:07] d0ghouse : season by season
[2022-07-08 13:34] thepcoffinator : I’ll just echo what <@459794188125339659> said but put it another way: the two skills listed as the player’s strongest skills in the flavor text on the player’s page are guaranteed to be the highest to max out. The one listed as weakest is guaranteed to be the lowest to max out. So you can gauge potential based on those. A player who has nothing maxed out yet is just risky and unpredictable. Also if you see that skills other than the listed weakest are maxed out at 4, then you know the weakest will max out at 4 also

[2022-07-16 22:06] d0ghouse : Not being able to set U21 lineup is deliberate by design. [2022-07-26 18:05] m_._b : Is there any penalty when C/LW plays as LW? What is the difference between C/LW and LW/C?
[2022-07-26 18:12] d0ghouse : No penalty. Difference is at the U21 level where the first position is seen as main position when deciding lineups.  **U21 and U17 Lineups** The U21 and U17 lineups are automatically created based on player ratings and positions. Note that some players have two positions. A ”main position” and a ”second position”. The system is set up in such a way that it first only considers main positions. Second positions are only considered if there are still lineup spots to be filled. For U17 teams, this is already taken into account when adding new youth players to the rosters. But in order to have an optimal U21 lineup, it is recommended to have enough players while ignoring second positions.
[2022-07-26 18:22] m_._b : thank you for the answer

His weakest talent will be endurance, meaning that it will be his weakest skill (Other skills can still tie this, as you can see END is 5 but DEF is 5). [2022-08-30 00:36] mr.president13 : To each their own of course. I think injuries add two really fun elements: first, the strategy - which I love most about these sim games. Suddenly, the cap becomes a lot more interesting. It gives me something more to look forward to each day because there’s a new unpredictable strategy element you have to be ready for. And second, the storytelling becomes more fun. That guy you thought would never make your team? Yeah well he just filled in for an injured player and was a PPG. Now what do you do? What story does that tell? Or your superstar went down in the playoffs but you still won it all - imagine the bragging rights you gain from saying I beat you without my best player? And the flip side, as much as it sucks, how do you spin the narrative and strategize when your superstar goes down and you were gunning for this year? Is next year still our year? To me, and I totally get it’s not for everybody and I respect that, it just adds so much depth to both ends of the game and I think that makes it really fun.

[2022-09-06 22:37] d0ghouse : Players gain 50% at U21 level and backup goalies 25% of starter goalies. So a backup goalie at PRO level gains 25% experience and a starter goalie at U21 level 50%.

[2022-09-06 22:40] d0ghouse : So to answer; starting in the minors gives the goalie more experience

[2022-09-28 10:28] euphael : how is overall skill of a player calculated?
[2022-09-28 11:01] hnadmin : By taking the average and counting every level above the average twice
[2022-09-28 11:18] euphael : What average? I meant that every ability growth results in growth of overall rating as well? Is experience takenninto account?
[2022-09-28 11:23] hnadmin : The average of the player's skills. Experience is not taken into account.
[2022-09-28 11:26] hnadmin : Example: Defenseman with 4 skills at 4 and 4 skills at 8. The sum of the skills is 48 and average is 6. Correction factor for above average skills is 8 (4x2). Corrected average is 56 divided by 8 = 7. Which stands for 70 overall rating.
[2022-09-28 11:35] euphael : got it, thank you for explaining 👍
[2022-09-28 11:37] rjs_lu_ridware_rangers : So the OVR increases more by training skills which are already above the players average skill rating?
[2022-09-28 11:39] hnadmin : correct
[2022-09-28 13:00] birdman6969 : How are decimals handled?

[2022-09-28 13:57] hnadmin : Decimals are taken into account. Just at the end of the formula rounded to nearest.
[2022-09-28 13:57] hnadmin : Yes that's correct

[2022-09-29 15:42] d0ghouse : The "main targets" always take priority. If they are no longer available (or not selected) only then it will look at your own ranking and auto-pick settings. If you selected a position you will draft that position unless there's no longer one available.
[2022-09-29 15:45] hnadmin : Depends on how you have set 'Only left defenseman'. If you have done it with the 'Position Limits' by setting LW,RW,C,RD and G to zero then your Main Targets who are not LD are not chosen. If you have done it by setting the Position Preference to LD then all of your Main Targets can be chosen. So basically Position Limits > Main Targets > Draft Ranking Order + Position Preference.

[2023-01-10 21:18] d0ghouse : Application forms of premium users are considered first: 1. In phase one, coaches are drawn for each nation filled in as ”first choice”. 2. Followed by draws with nations filled in as ”second choice” and ”third choice”. 3.
